bullets.title: CPI Print Today: Fed's Waller Signals 50bp Hike Risk if Core ≥0.3% MoM
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller surprised markets by signaling a potential 50bp December hike if October core CPI prints at/above 0.3% MoM, hawkish given recent FCI tightening from equities. Street consensus sits at +0.23% MoM core (3.2% YoY) with JPM's Feroli at +0.23%/+0.25% headline; a 0.2% or below print is viewed as risk-on while 0.3%+ would be risk-off. Market pricing December FOMC hike odds near 100% with March at ~80%.

bullets.title: Systematic Washout Sets Up Re-Risking: Risk Control at Lowest Since Tariff Shock
bullets.body: Risk Control exposure hit 55% (lowest since tariff lows) and CTA equity exposure turned negative at -5%, a bottoming signal historically. UBS estimates ~$365bn of systematic selling cleared last week from Risk Control, CTAs, and levered ETFs; real-money demand is stepping in with Hyperscalers +2.3std and Software +2.1std buying on Monday. JPM notes leverage reset from 100th to 76th percentile with vol targeters still having ~$50bn left to sell.

bullets.title: S&P +2.3%, Nasdaq +3.4% Monday on Tech/AI Rotation; Semis +8%, Optical +9%
bullets.body: Monday saw a broad risk-on rebound led by AI infrastructure names — Semis +8%, Optical +9%, Memory +7% — as HF rotation back into AI had real sponsorship with S&P/Nasdaq excess buying of $34bn/$60bn by 1pm. Mega-caps (GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN, META, AAPL) all added ~50bps while quants cut another -0.7std, suggesting more deleveraging ahead. Pre-market Tuesday is essentially flat (SPX futs +0.0% at 7574) with 10yr yield up 3bps to 4.90%.

bullets.title: NVDA: CEO Scandal, Export Controls, and BofA US-1 Removal Create Multi-Layered Overhang
bullets.body: NVDA shed ~$200bn market cap (-4.5%) Monday on a confluence of negatives: FBI inquiry into Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a Chinese intelligence-linked executive enabling $7.5B+ chip shipments, White House considering new advanced chip export controls to China, and legal chief's alleged intervention in a Commerce Dept smuggling probe. BofA removed NVDA (along with MU and LRCX) from its US 1 List while maintaining Buy; Mizuho cut PT to $250 from $315 and Citi trimmed to $285 from prior on 19x vs 21x P/E. AMD +13% and semicap +6.85% as competitors reportedly seize market share opportunities.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Sector Volatility Elevated: SMH IV 44.9, RV 68.6; Put-Call Skew at 83rd %ile
bullets.body: SMH fell 11% the week of Nov 5 following midterm elections, with implied vol at 44.9 (76th percentile) and realized vol at 68.6 (97th percentile) — the 23.7pt spread flags ongoing downside risk. Investor put-call skew in the 83rd percentile relative to 1Y, reflecting deeply bearish positioning. VIX fell 1.2pts to 19.9 on declining constituent correlation but investors anticipate a further rise.

bullets.title: Midterm Outcome: Data Center Permitting Headwind Emerges as 2028+ Risk
bullets.body: Governor-elect Hinojosa's win raises state-level regulatory risk for data centers — 30-40% of US data center capacity is forecasted for Texas and faces slower approvals. JPM notes 2027 AI capex (~$1.5T) is largely insulated as projects are already funded and under construction, but the growth curve is likely to flatten into 2028+ as permitting becomes more difficult. Each $100bn in capex translates to ~$9 for S&P EPS (~2.5% earnings growth); at $1.5T that adds ~$18 EPS or 4-5% to 2027 growth.

bullets.title: Iran De-Escalation Drives Oil -4%; WTI Below $85, Brent Below $90
bullets.body: Trump signaled further Iran military strikes 'highly unlikely' after Qatar PM meeting, triggering a ~4% oil decline Monday with WTI extending losses to -2.4% pre-market Tuesday at $84.76 and Brent slipping below $90 for the first time since August. National gasoline average fell below $4.00/gallon to $3.978. Separately, Ukraine-Russia peace talks began with narrowing gaps per reports.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO (ANT) Launches at $70-78/sh, ~$61B Raise; $26B Tech Cornerstone Placement
bullets.body: Anthropic filed an amended S-1 for 825M Class A shares at $70-78/sh (97% primary), implying a ~$61B public raise with estimated total market cap near $1T at the top of the range — down from prior $1.5-2.0T expectations. Seven tech giants (AMD, AVGO, GOOGL, MU, MSFT, NVDA, TSMC) committed $26B in a concurrent private Class N placement at IPO price. Pricing expected post-close November 18; trading begins November 19.

bullets.title: Tactical Rotation: Hyperscalers Preferred Over Picks-and-Shovels AI Plays
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (JPM, UBS) are calling for a tactical shift toward hyperscalers and away from picks-and-shovels AI names given ongoing financing, monetization, and valuation challenges in the latter. UBS targets SPX 8,900 by end-2027 on $490 2028 EPS, with NVDA/MU/AVGO accounting for ~45% of 2027 SPX EPS growth. AI momentum index has faded over 9 consecutive sessions with AI-adjacent multiples compressing ~35% since May (Semis -52%, Memory -60%, Hyperscalers -14%).

bullets.title: TSMC October Revenue +59.7% YoY to $17.9B; Q4 Expected +15% QoQ on N3/N2 Ramp
bullets.body: TSMC reported October monthly revenue of NT$586.6-586.9B (+59.7% YoY, ~$17.9B), tracking well ahead for Q4 guidance of $52.3-54.3B — implying ~15% QoQ growth — driven by N3 AI accelerators/CPUs and an accelerating N2 ramp. Analyst consensus implies 63% Q4 growth, signaling resilient AI demand. TSMC also approved a $40.9B capex budget.

bullets.title: NFIB October: Small Biz Price-Raising Plans Jump to July 2022 Highs; Compensation Plans Rise
bullets.body: NFIB small business optimism edged down 0.1pt to 97.8 (third straight monthly decline) but price-raising plans surged 6pts to net 37% — the highest since July 2022 — and actual price increases rose to net 33%, historically very elevated. Compensation plans hit their highest level since December 2025, flagging wage inflation risk into 2027. Taxes surged 10pts to 21% as the top concern, supply chain disruptions at 65% (highest since June), and short-term loan rates rose to 8.5%.

bullets.title: MSFT Lobbying to Block Chinese Optical Transceiver Ban; Data Center Supply Chain at Risk
bullets.body: Microsoft has been actively lobbying the Trump administration to abandon a planned FCC/White House ban on Chinese optical transceivers, arguing it would slow US data center construction. Separately, the White House is considering new NVDA advanced chip export controls and Chinese firm Moonshot AI reportedly accessed NVDA B300 GPUs via a 432M yuan server contract despite existing restrictions. MSFT has 35 US data centers under construction and 134 more planned.

bullets.title: Gold +3% Post-Midterms; JPM Sees Bullish Window Opening with Potential $4,500+ in 2027
bullets.body: Gold rose ~3% post-election with JPM flagging a bullish window expected to open over coming months and potential upside above $4,500/oz in 2027. However, Hedgeye notes gold failed at the $4,096 trade level, flagging sensitivity to short-end rates and USD; front-end rates popped to 4.61% on CPI acceleration. Copper faces headwinds from AI buildout uncertainty and US tariff follow-through, though Chinese tightness provides a support floor.

bullets.title: Data Center Power Constraints Tightening: 20% CAGR to 300GW by 2030, 2026-28 Shortfall Anticipated
bullets.body: MS/Morgan Stanley flags AI infrastructure constraints shifting beyond initial bottlenecks to behind-the-meter power hurdles, with data center capacity expected to grow ~20% CAGR to 300+ GW by 2030 and a 2026-2028 power shortfall anticipated. AI data centers have increased industrial electricity prices ~5.4 $/MWh on average. Data center operators are sourcing used turbines and jet engines for power; Norway is restricting new data center expansion.

bullets.title: JPM YE26 SPX Target 8,000 (8.4% Upside); October Was Largest Single-Month Long Momentum Unwind on Record
bullets.body: JPM's Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 at $365 EPS and 21.9x, implying ~8.4% upside. October saw the largest single-month Long Momentum unwind in history (~11%, ~6 std deviations) with AI multiples compressing ~35% since May. Goldman similarly remains overweight equities over 3-12 months, citing lighter positioning and lower valuations supporting risk assets into year-end.

bullets.title: CSCO F1Q27 Preview: Beat-and-Raise Expected on AI Networking; FY27 AI Revenue Target Raised to $8.5B
bullets.body: JPM reiterates Overweight on CSCO with $150 PT, forecasting F1Q27 revenue of $18.4B vs. guidance of $18.1B and expecting FY27 AI revenue guidance to raise to ~$8.5B (+100%+ growth) from $7.5B prior. FY27 overall revenue guidance seen lifting to +16-17% from +15%, with networking growth at 40%+ YoY in F1Q27. Stock is down 17% from its October peak to $98.65, bringing NTM multiple to 18-19x — a more palatable entry.

bullets.title: AVGO Confirmed as Sole Supplier for Google TPU Roadmap Through 2028+
bullets.body: AVGO's roadmap is described as unchallenged: Google's v8i Max TPU (2x compute, 2H27 ramp) and v9.5/v10 2nm SKU (mid-2028 production) align with AVGO's September roadmap with no TPU revenue growth slowdown expected through CY31. JPM and other sources confirm AVGO as supplier for Google's most performant TPU programs, providing long-duration visibility.

bullets.title: MSFT Azure at 48% CC Growth; Ignite Conference to Showcase Full-Stack AI Integration
bullets.body: RBC flags MSFT Azure accelerating to 48% constant-currency growth with the upcoming Ignite conference expected to showcase full-stack AI integration across infrastructure, applications, and security. IBM and Microsoft also jointly launched 'Imagine Enterprise,' an agentic AI platform for industry-specific transformation with forward-deployed engineering support.

bullets.title: NVDA Earnings Preview: ~$109B Oct-Q Expected; 2028 Backlog Visibility Is Key Investor Focus
bullets.body: Citi forecasts NVDA Oct-Q revenue of ~$109B vs. $108B guide with modest EPS beat ($2.52 vs. $2.49 consensus), and Jan-Q at $125B (+15% QoQ) on Rubin ramp. Jan-Q gross margins guided at 71.5% vs. Street 72.1% due to HBM price increases and early Rubin costs. The key investor debate has shifted to 2028 order visibility and backlog conversion, with CEO investigation creating a leadership stability overhang; PT trimmed from 21x to 19x P/E.

bullets.title: Inflation Regime Concern: September CPI Was Third Upside Surprise in 12 Releases; 2Y Yield ~25bp Too Low
bullets.body: September CPI was the third upside surprise in the last 12 releases and the largest since March 2024; inflation data has surprised to the upside most frequently since May 2021 per JPM. The 2Y yield is flagged as ~25bp too low relative to model-based valuation with the yield curve expected to flatten near-term. NFIB small biz data adds to concern with price-raising plans at July 2022 highs and compensation plans rising, flagging persistent domestic inflation pressure.
